references.text: Basic principle that vows and oaths must be kept, which verse 14 builds upon with the husband's right to confirm or annul them
Parallel situation where a husband may annul his wife's vows on the day he hears about them
Direct context explaining that a husband can confirm or annul vows involving self-denial
Background for the husband's authority over his wife in marriage
The importance of keeping vows made to the Lord, emphasizing the seriousness of oaths and vows
Warning against making vows and the importance of fulfilling them
Self-denial and fasting as expressions of humility, relevant to 'afflicting oneself'
Command to afflict oneself on the Day of Atonement, using the same expression found in verse 14
New Testament perspective on the husband's role as head of the wife in marriage
New Testament teaching about the wife's submission to her husband
